Definition: a star (as round or as shining); figuratively, a prince
BiblicalUsage: Stars are the lights God set in the heavens, and Scripture uses them three ways: as the countless multitude of Abraham's seed in Deuteronomy 1:10, as the rulers and powers of the age, and as the shining of the righteous. Balaam's prophecy in Numbers 24:17 says "there shall come a Star out of Jacob," Daniel 12:3 promises those who turn many to righteousness will shine "as the stars for ever and ever," and Amos 5:26 warns Israel for worshipping "the star of your god."
TheologicalSignificance: To my mind, the stars preach both ways: they declare God's power and His promises, and they expose the folly of worshipping the creation instead of the Creator who hung them there. I look up at the stars and remember that the God who hung them there also promised to multiply His people like them.
